title: Oracle WebLogic 14c for C2M — Install, Configure & Domain Setup
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (Oracle Utilities C2M + WebLogic 14c administration; middleware/database/integration work, production-impact care).

Oracle Utilities C2M/CC&B/MDM + WebLogic 14c authored from Oracle's official product + OUAF docs; version-specific details (C2M 25.4/min v2.9, WebLogic 14c) cited or flagged 'verify for your version'; My-Oracle-Support-gated patches/notes are pointed to, not reproduced. Automation is WLST (Jython)/shell/SQL, not PowerShell.
hook: Build the WebLogic 14c foundation C2M runs on
problem: Oracle Utilities C2M runs on Oracle WebLogic Server — and a mis-built domain undermines everything above it. This solution installs and configures WebLogic 14c for C2M: the domain, Administration Server and managed servers, Node Manager, data sources, and the JVM/startup configuration C2M expects — the middleware foundation, done right and pilot-first.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — WebLogic 14c for C2M: domain topology, Admin/managed servers, Node Manager, data sources, and how OUAF sits on the domain.
Requirements Guide — each prerequisite with how to verify/implement (certified WebLogic 14c + JDK, OS product account, DB connectivity, C2M entitlement).

Implementation Guide — exact steps to install WebLogic 14c, create the named domain, configure Admin/managed servers + Node Manager, set up data sources, tune JVM/startup, and validate the domain, pilot-first.

5 automation scripts (WLST/Jython, shell & SQL) — environment/config discovery, per-node validation, a health/coverage report, safe remediation (dry-run by default), and a scope/target helper — authentic to C2M & WebLogic administration.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides (domain up, managed servers running, data sources healthy) plus Best Practices for domain layout and Node Manager.
short: Install and configure Oracle WebLogic 14c for C2M — domain, Admin/managed servers, Node Manager, data sources, JVM/startup — the middleware foundation, pilot-first. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
